perItemFindings.one_line: Delivered tier subfield < floor field; not salvageable within scope.

verbatim_critique: [D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=subfield below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The delivered results establish sharp closures through positive-slack branch pruning and unrestricted-cone duality, an all-arm extension conditional on nonemptiness, a robust strict-improvement example, boundary discontinuity with an exact known-pair lower result, and finite-sample projection coverage. They do not deliver the adaptive contracting procedure or matching general boundary rate posed in oeq:boundary-adaptive-inference, and the statistical lower result is confined to a constructed SDC two-point experiment. The TL;DR's phrase "covers the whole exact set" slightly overstates the theorem, which covers the sharp closure of an identified set that need not itself be closed under exact-support restrictions. The leading-journal score is constrained by the fixed finite grid, known support endpoints, conservative binary-treatment inference, and absence of an actual reanalysis demonstrating how much the support-filtered set changes the cited applications. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.6 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
